title_en: Answers on the exegesis of certain verses
body_en:
Exegesis of: {O you who believe, be conscious of God and speak a word that is right}.

This question is about the exegesis of God Most High's words: {O you who believe, be conscious of God and speak a word that is right; He will set right your deeds for you and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys God and His Messenger has attained a mighty attainment} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:70–71).

God, glorified and exalted, has commanded us to be conscious of Him, and to speak a word that is right — which is the speaking of the truth — and not to speak what is false; and He made clear the good that follows upon that, namely that if we do so He sets our affairs right for us and grants us Paradise. So He said: "He will set right your deeds for you and forgive you your sins." "And whoever obeys God and His Messenger" in what God has commanded and His Messenger has commanded, or what God has forbidden or His Messenger has forbidden, "has attained a mighty attainment", by his obedience to God and His Messenger.

------------------------------------

Exegesis of: {and you will not be asked about the companions of the Blaze}.

[What do you say] about the exegesis of God Most High's words: {and you will not be asked about the companions of the Blaze}?

This verse has two readings. One is {wa-lā tusʾalu ʿan aṣḥāb al-jaḥīm} and the other is {wa-lā tasʾal ʿan aṣḥāb al-jaḥīm} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:119). As for the reading wa-lā tasʾal ʿan aṣḥāb al-jaḥīm — that is, let their affair not trouble you, for they are in the utmost of the abiding, perpetual punishment. And as for wa-lā tusʾalu ʿan aṣḥāb al-jaḥīm — that is, that you are not held to account for their disobedience, for every person is answerable for his own sin and no one else is asked about it..

flags.arabic: ما عن تفسير قول الله تعالى
flags.context: the opening of the second question
options: [What do you say] about the exegesis of ...
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT. The Arabic as printed, mā ʿan tafsīr, is not grammatical; a word has dropped out, most probably qawlukum ('what do you say about') or a similar formula, which the first question's phrasing supports. The English marks the supply in square brackets rather than making it silently. body_ar preserves the defect.

flags.context: the two canonical readings of the verse
options: give both readings transliterated, with a distinct English rendering for each
give both readings in Arabic only and one English rendering
give one reading in English and footnote the other
flags.note: The whole answer turns on a difference of vocalisation that cannot be shown in an English translation of the verse: tusʾalu is passive, 'you are not asked', while tasʾal is an imperative, 'do not ask'. The heading and the question quote the verse unvocalised, so the English heading has had to choose one; it uses the passive, which is the majority reading, and the answer then sets out both. A reviewer should decide whether the site's Qur'an display can carry vocalised Arabic for cases like this, which will recur throughout the qirāʾāt material.

flags.context: the gloss on the imperative reading
options: let their affair not trouble you
do not concern yourself with their affair
their affair is not your concern
flags.note: The Arabic is a jussive and the sense is that the Prophet is not to be grieved over their fate. Option 2 turns it into a statement rather than an instruction and would blur the very distinction between the two readings that the answer exists to draw.

translator_notes: TYPING DECISION. The source presents this page as 'answers' (ajwibah) to questions put to the Sheikh, in the same question-and-answer form as the written fatwas. It is typed 'article' rather than 'fatwa' because it contains no ruling on an act: the glossary fixes fatwā as 'a considered legal opinion', and this page is explanatory. The site must not display it as a fatwa, or readers will take its contents for rulings.
Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

In the source, the answer begins with the elliptical particle 'anna ('[the answer is] that ...'), the Joomla fatwa template's standing form. The English drops the particle and begins the sentence directly; no content is added or removed by this.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off and the full material is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.
This page is a compilation of two separate answers, divided in the source by a row of hyphens, kept in both body_ar and body_en.
'The companions of the Blaze' renders aṣḥāb al-jaḥīm. Al-jaḥīm is one of the names of the Fire.

The verse references have been supplied per house style; the source gives the verse texts alone. The verse quoted in the first answer's heading is the opening of Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:70, and the full quotation runs to the end of 33:71.

Both answers keep the Sheikh's practice of re-quoting fragments of the verse inside his own sentences; those re-quotations are rendered in ordinary quotation marks rather than brace brackets, since he is citing rather than presenting the verse.
